title: 7-Nitroindazole reduces L-DOPA-induced dyskinesias in non-human Parkinsonian primate.
rationale: Three MPTP macaques received 7-nitroindazole in subcutaneous peanut-oil solution with levodopa; one had resting tremor in disease history. Dyskinesia comparison concerns drug addition, not oral peanut oil: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10188238/

title: Odor-Specific Symptoms in Parkinson's Disease-UPSIT-TC Odor Identification Status Versus Clinical Severity.
rationale: Taiwanese Parkinson cohort uses grapefruit as a scratch-and-sniff odor identification cue; motor tremor scores combine rest with postural and kinetic items. Neither oral fruit exposure nor its effect on resting tremor was tested. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13687933/

title: UPSIT subitems may predict motor progression in Parkinson's disease.
rationale: Parkinson longitudinal study treats grapefruit as an odor-identification test item; its motor progression analysis is a composite, not a fruit intervention or isolated rest-tremor outcome. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10625917/

title: What does it mean when the pleasant smells come and go? Correlation between UPSIT odor identification status and fluctuation of non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease.
rationale: Longitudinal Parkinson olfactory testing uses a grapefruit odor cue, not oral fruit assignment; it does not estimate a grapefruit intake effect on rest tremor. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12014810/

title: The greatest loss of unpleasant smells may be related to the risk of more severe PD symptoms.
rationale: Parkinson odor-valence study excludes grapefruit among five odors from the valence analyses; its pooled tremor includes MDS-UPDRS items 3.15–3.18. Neither grapefruit ingestion nor an isolated rest-tremor effect is tested. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11018954/

title: Evaluation of Simvastatin as a Disease-Modifying Treatment for Patients With Parkinson Disease: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
rationale: Simvastatin trial excluded participants unable to abstain from grapefruit products; its assigned comparison was simvastatin versus placebo, not eating versus avoiding grapefruit. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9623477/

title: The predictive value of SS-16 in clinically diagnosed Parkinson's disease patients: comparison with (99m)Tc-TRODAT-1 SPECT scans.
rationale: Parkinson diagnostic olfaction study retained the original Sniffin Sticks odors while translating the grapefruit response description to pomelo; no grapefruit food intervention or separate intake-related rest-tremor effect. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40035-016-0062-4

title: PF-06649751 efficacy and safety in early Parkinson's disease: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
rationale: PF-06649751 versus placebo trial prohibited grapefruit and related citrus during treatment; safety observations cannot establish a fruit effect. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7066585/

title: Combination of olfactory test and substantia nigra transcranial sonopraphy in the differential diagnosis of Parkinson's disease: a pilot study from China.
rationale: The 37 Parkinson and 26 essential tremor participants underwent odor identification and diagnostic imaging. Methods retain original odors but translate the grapefruit descriptor to pomelo; no edible grapefruit exposure or rest-tremor intervention. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/2047-9158-1-25

title: A non-invasive olfactory bulb measure dissociates Parkinson's patients from healthy controls and discloses disease duration.
rationale: Parkinson olfactory bulb imaging exposes participants to grapefruit essential-oil odor as a sensory cue, rather than testing oral fruit intake or a fruit-related rest-tremor comparison. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8373926/

title: Concurrent administration of donepezil HCl and levodopa/carbidopa in patients with Parkinson's disease: assessment of pharmacokinetic changes and safety following multiple oral doses.
rationale: Donepezil and levodopa study prohibited grapefruit-containing foods during site attendance; it did not assign or compare grapefruit intake. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1884553/

title: Odor-Specific Symptoms in Parkinson's Disease-UPSIT-TC Odor Identification Status Versus Clinical Severity.
rationale: Retrospective Parkinson olfactory study: the Taiwanese UPSIT replaced the original dill-pickle odor with rubber tire; no dill ingestion comparison. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13687933/

title: Selective hyposmia in Parkinson disease: association with hippocampal dopamine activity.
rationale: Dill pickle is one of three UPSIT odor-identification cues in PD, correlated with brain dopamine imaging; not dried dill eaten or an intervention on rest tremor. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2634293/

title: Variants in the proteasome regulator PSMF1 cause a phenotypic spectrum from parkinsonism to perinatal lethality.
rationale: PSMF1 genetic parkinsonism study; corn oil is injected control in a mouse tamoxifen experiment, not oral dietary corn oil or a PD rest-tremor comparison. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13376622/

title: Dietary habits and adherence to the Mediterranean diet in a cohort of Parkinson's disease patients in Lithuania.
rationale: The food-frequency case-control study reports olive oil used in cooking and Mediterranean adherence. The grade and isolated rest-tremor estimate are unreported.

title: Insulin Resistance and Metabolic Dysfunction in Early-Stage Parkinson's Disease: Evidence from a Preliminary Case-Control Study.
rationale: Olive oil is a component of the Mediterranean diet screener in the metabolic case-control study. No graded oil comparison or separate rest-tremor severity outcome.

title: A randomized safety and feasibility crossover trial of two Mediterranean-ketogenic interventions in individuals with Parkinson's disease.
rationale: Both randomized diet periods emphasize ungraded olive oil. Table 3 gives nonspecific tremor exacerbations; no separate rest item or oil-only arm.

title: A prebiotic dietary pilot intervention restores faecal metabolites and may be neuroprotective in Parkinson's Disease.
rationale: Bedarf diet included apple and ungraded olive oil with other foods and lactulose. The paper and supplement give Part III totals and no rest item or single-food comparison.

title: Dietary approach to stop hypertension (DASH), but not Mediterranean and MIND, dietary pattern protects against Parkinson's disease.
rationale: Reported oil intake contributes to multicomponent diet scores. The Parkinson comparison is based on case status and motor scales, with no separate rest item related to the oil.

title: Exploring the Facilitators and Barriers of Adherence to Mediterranean-Ketogenic Dietary Interventions in Parkinson's Disease: A Qualitative Study.
rationale: Qualitative report from the same KIM family. Olive oil appears in the shared diet and interview context. No independent cohort or oil-to-rest outcome.

title: Cannabidiol-enriched cannabis extraction product in Parkinson's disease: A randomized, double-blind, and placebo-controlled trial in Buriram Hospital.
rationale: Both study groups received an olive-oil vehicle. The difference is cannabinoid content and the original reports total motor examination rather than an oil-specific rest item.

title: A Phase Ib, Double Blind, Randomized Study of Cannabis Oil for Pain in Parkinson's Disease.
rationale: The paper describes olive oil as carrier in all three cannabinoid-ratio study formulations. Pain and global motor results do not identify an olive-grade or separate rest-tremor effect.

title: Mediterranean Diet Adherence in People With Parkinson's Disease Reduces Constipation Symptoms and Changes Fecal Microbiota After a 5-Week Single-Arm Pilot Study.
rationale: Single-arm constipation trial advises olive oil in a whole dietary pattern. No isolated olive-oil treatment or separate rest-tremor result.

title: Current understanding of the molecular mechanisms in Parkinson's disease: Targets for potential treatments.
rationale: Narrative review lists olive lignan sources and resting tremor in different contexts. No original oral culinary comparison in this record.

title: Longitudinal assessment of the association between pesticide exposure and lifestyle with Parkinson's disease motor severity.
rationale: Black tea is a questionnaire exposure. A smaller LRRK2 subgroup shows a favorable association on the patient-rated motor composite; no examination rest item is reported.

title: Blood profile holds clues to role of infection in a premonitory state for idiopathic parkinsonism and of gastrointestinal infection in established disease.
rationale: Black tea, coffee or water are breakfast options for breath testing. Rest and postural tremor are described separately in clinical findings without a beverage-specific comparison.

title: The Indian Smell Identification Test for Parkinson's Disease: Limitations of Binary Scoring and Proposal of a Modified Graded Approach.
rationale: PD olfaction study presents cardamom odor on a cotton bud for identification; two cohorts assess smell, not ground cardamom ingestion or rest-tremor effects. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13349266/

title: A prebiotic dietary pilot intervention restores faecal metabolites and may be neuroprotective in Parkinson's Disease.
rationale: Bedarf diet included apple and ungraded olive oil with other foods and lactulose. The paper and supplement give Part III totals and no rest item or single-food comparison.

title: Cortical oscillatory dysfunction in Parkinson disease during movement activation and inhibition.
rationale: NUTMEG is the name of neuroimaging analysis software, not the spice; the PD movement-inhibition study excludes persistent tremor and does not study nutmeg intake. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8896690/
